<h1 class="h1">Probabilistic Machine Learning</h1>
<p class="role">ES 661 · IIT Gandhinagar · Semester I, 2023–24</p>
<p class="lede" style="margin-top:18px">ES 661 is a course on probabilistic machine learning: Bayesian inference, estimation, sampling, approximate inference, probabilistic models, and their use in Bayesian optimisation and active learning. Lectures link their recordings, slides, cheat sheets and notebooks.</p>

<div class="two rule-top">
<section id="faq"><h2>Questions</h2>
<details class="q" id="grading"><summary>How is the course graded?</summary><p>Three quizzes (36%), four assignments (32%), a group project (27%) and an interactive article (5%). See <a href="assessment.html#grading">Grading</a>.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="quizzes"><summary>When are the quizzes?</summary><p>There are three quizzes of 12% each, held in the exam 1, 2 and 3 slots.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="assignments"><summary>How do the assignments work?</summary><p>Each assignment is a single Jupyter notebook done in a group, using PyTorch and <code>torch.distributions</code>, with about a week to complete it. Each is followed by a viva and graded on correctness of the code (50%), code quality (25%) and presentation and conceptual understanding (25%).</p></details>
<details class="q" id="project"><summary>Is there a project?</summary><p>Yes, in groups of three to five students. It has a first presentation, a final presentation and a final report. See <a href="assessment.html#project">Project</a>.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="interactive-article"><summary>What is the interactive article?</summary><p>A Streamlit app or similar interactive article that explains a concept from the course. See the course's <a href="interactive-apps.html">interactive apps</a>.</p></details>
<p class="small muted" style="margin-top:12px">Ask anything else on <a href="https://join.slack.com/t/pml23/shared_invite/zt-20o47q69t-SRBCc6sbNybppafChg8rPA">the course Slack</a>.</p>
</section>
<section id="topics"><h2>Main topics</h2>
<ol class="refs">
  <li>Bayesian inference</li>
  <li>Estimation: maximum likelihood, maximum a posteriori, full Bayesian</li>
  <li>Sampling: rejection sampling, Monte Carlo, specific sampling techniques such as Box–Muller</li>
  <li>Approximate inference: variational inference, Markov chain Monte Carlo, Laplace approximation</li>
  <li>Models: Bayesian linear and logistic regression, Bayesian neural networks, Gaussian processes, probabilistic PCA</li>
  <li>Applications: Bayesian optimisation, active learning</li>
</ol>
</section>
</div>
